mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is persistently below its long-run average, the real interest rate is expected to decline, lowering discount rates and increasing the present value of expected corporate cash flows, thereby driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically higher than the 30-day moving average of the same period in the prior 12 months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in unemployment claims (PAYEMS) indicates weakening labor market strength, which typically precedes a decline in consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day and 60-day forward returns both show positive excess returns over the prior 30-day window (p < 0.05 two-tailed).

mechanism_narrative: Rising industrial production (INDPRO) suggests expanding economic demand for goods, which is associated with stronger corporate earnings forecasts and higher equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward return is negative and INDPRO growth is not statistically significant (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2% suggests the Federal Reserve may hold rates steady or cut, reducing financing costs for equities and increasing expected future earnings, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward return is flat or negative despite CPIAUCSL meeting the trigger condition (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising unemployment (UNRATE) and persistent weakness in retail activity (HOUST) jointly signal a loss of monetary policy credibility, prompting investors to discount future earnings more aggressively and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 6.5% AND HOUST < 700 for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward return is positive and both UNRATE and HOUST show recovery (UNRATE > 7%, HOUST > 750) within the next 2 months (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden surge in manufacturing payrolls (RSAFS) above expectations suggests resilient labor demand, which can boost consumer spending and corporate profits, resulting in positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward return is negative and RSAFS does not sustain above 350000 for the following 2 months (p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS exceeds 5%, it signals a tightening cycle that raises real borrowing costs, reducing the present value of expected equity cash flows and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward return is positive and FEDFUNDS reverts to below 5% within 2 months (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) coupled with a sharp drop in industrial production (INDPRO) suggests weakening demand, lowering growth expectations and resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 198 AND INDPRO < 102 for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day forward return is positive and both CPIAUCSL and INDPRO rebound above their prior month averages (p < 0.05).
